page: OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud instance configured with an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs without hyperthreading, paired with 84 GB of system memory, which yields 5.25 GB per core. Acceleration is handled by three NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs based on the Turing microarchitecture, delivering an aggregated 48 GB of GDDR6 VRAM across the three cards. Local storage includes a 400 GB SSD, and networking is provisioned at a 10 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute performance, particularly in machine learning execution. In large language model inference benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results in prompt processing across small 135M, medium 7B, and large 70B models, reaching up to 8884.89 tokens per second on smaller architectures. General-purpose CPU metrics from Geekbench 6 and PassMark reflect mid-range single-core and multi-core output, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8459.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 20742.83. Memory read bandwidth is competitive, evidenced by a strong PassMark memory rating of 2913.07, though uncached large-block write bandwidth and single-threaded gzip compression register in lower percentiles.

The triple-GPU topology presents high compute density for parallel graphical and mathematical operations, delivering solid cost efficiency for inference and rendering tasks compared to procuring separate single-GPU nodes. The architectural tradeoff centers on sequential write performance and mid-tier single-threaded CPU speed, which are less suitable for IOPS-bound transactional databases. The rtx5000-84 is best suited for distributed deep learning inference, batch image processing, ray-tracing workloads, and multi-stream computer vision pipelines.
description: OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a GPU-focused cloud instance featuring an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz, 84 GB of RAM, and three NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs providing 48 GB of total VRAM. Storage is provisioned via a 400 GB local SSD alongside a 10 Gbps network baseline. Performance benchmarks reveal top-tier prompt processing and generation speeds across small, medium, and large language models, supported by strong PassMark memory ratings. CPU compute and uncached memory writes reflect standard mid-tier throughput, making the instance less suited for write-heavy relational databases. Instead, its multi-GPU architecture delivers dense parallel execution and efficient resource scaling for machine learning inference, computer vision, 3D rendering, and batch image analysis.
